newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on arbitrage play.

text.p: * Peso average at 26.255 from 26.243 to the dollar
The Philippine peso weakened on Friday to close at 26.263 from 26.244 on interest rate arbitrage play by banks for the weekend, traders said.

The peso's value was pulled down by a four-day swap point taking into account the interest rate premium of the peso over the dollar and the fact that Monday would be a holiday in New York, they said. "The market was trading at value today and value Tuesday," one dealer said.

Essentially, he said, banks were buying dollars for delivery on Tuesday to recover the dollars they sold for same-day delivery. In this way, banks have the pesos that would earn a higher interest for the weekend.

The peso started weak at 26.266 and hit a day-low of 26.27 pesos after the Central Bank gave a cue to the market that allowed a higher dollar rate when it raised its offer rate for the dollar to 26.272 from the previous day's 26.25 pesos, one trader said.
"But some banks, long on dollars, started selling their dollars," said the same trader.
The peso hit a day-high of 26.240 pesos before the Central Bank stepped in to buy about $23 million at 26.242 to 26.243 pesos, traders said.
Later, the peso just traded within the lower range of 26.262 to 26.268 pesos, traders said.
Turnover was higher at $174.90 million from $146.80 million.
On Monday, traders said the peso could trade in the 26.25 to 26.28 peso-range, the Central Bank's desired band.
